about: cesr.parse cases that must be rejected, each a well-formed stream (a genus/version code, a KERI 2.0 inception framed by its version string, attachments) with exactly one thing broken. The specification states almost no parser-side rejection rule. Where it states the rule (line 1129), the assertion keeps that clause's level; where the rejection is only inferred from a producer-side MUST, the assertion is graded SHOULD and records the inference in inferred_from.

cases.title: Reject a stream that ends inside a signature
cases.description: A KERI 2.0 inception, then an attachments group holding a -K of one signature, with the last two bytes of the stream removed. The -C and -K sizes promise 22 quadlets of signature and the stream holds 21.5. The adapter protocol makes the end of the input final (a harness rule, not a specification claim), so a parser may not wait for more bytes. The specification states no parser-side rule for this stream; the stream breaks the cited MUST, and the assertion that a parser rejects it is graded SHOULD on the inference recorded in inferred_from.

assertions.note: Relies on the adapter protocol's end-of-input rule. Informative class: truncated.

cases.title: Reject a signature group whose size ends it inside a signature
cases.description: Inside an attachments group, a -K of size 21 holds an 88-character (22-quadlet) signature: -K ends four characters before the signature does, and those four characters then sit inside -C where no element can start. The specification states no parser-side rule for this stream; the stream breaks the cited MUST, and the assertion that a parser rejects it is graded SHOULD on the inference recorded in inferred_from.

cases.title: Reject a stream that ends inside a small count code
cases.description: After a KERI 2.0 inception the stream holds only -CA, three characters of a four-character count code. The adapter protocol makes the end of the input final (a harness rule, not a specification claim), so a parser may not wait for more bytes. The specification states no parser-side rule for this stream; the stream breaks the cited MUST, and the assertion that a parser rejects it is graded SHOULD on the inference recorded in inferred_from.

assertions.note: Relies on the adapter protocol's end-of-input rule. Informative class: truncated.

cases.title: Reject a stream that ends inside a large count code
cases.description: After a KERI 2.0 inception the stream holds only --CAAA, six characters of an eight-character count code. The adapter protocol makes the end of the input final (a harness rule, not a specification claim), so a parser may not wait for more bytes. The specification states no parser-side rule for this stream; the stream breaks the cited MUST, and the assertion that a parser rejects it is graded SHOULD on the inference recorded in inferred_from.

assertions.note: Relies on the adapter protocol's end-of-input rule. Informative class: truncated.

cases.title: Reject an attachment count code whose second character selects no defined table
cases.description: After a KERI 2.0 inception, the attachment position holds the count code -0AB, whose second character is the numeral 0. The specification reserves numerals for other count code tables and genus 2.00 defines none, so the code is an error. (keripy 1.x used -0 as its big-count selector; genus 2.00 uses --.) The clause calls the code an error but does not say what a parser does with it, so the assertion that a parser rejects the stream is graded SHOULD on the inference recorded in inferred_from.

cases.title: Reject an indexed signature whose pad bits are not zero
cases.description: An A# indexed signature, in a -K after a KERI 2.0 inception, whose pad bits between the index and the value are not zero. The raw value bits are untouched. The specification states no parser-side rule for this stream; the stream breaks the cited MUST, and the assertion that a parser rejects it is graded SHOULD on the inference recorded in inferred_from.

cases.title: Reject a primitive whose pad bits are not zero
cases.description: A nontransferable receipt couple whose B prefix carries a 1 in the two bits that come from its zero lead byte. The specification states no parser-side rule for this stream; the stream breaks the cited MUST, and the assertion that a parser rejects it is graded SHOULD on the inference recorded in inferred_from.

cases.title: Reject a binary-domain signature whose pad bits are not zero
cases.description: A binary-domain attachments group whose A# signature has nonzero pad bits between its index and value. The specification states no parser-side rule for this stream; the stream breaks the cited MUST, and the assertion that a parser rejects it is graded SHOULD on the inference recorded in inferred_from.

cases.title: Reject a stream that resumes with a bare primitive
cases.description: After a KERI 2.0 inception and its attachments group, the stream continues with a D key and no count code. Its first byte, 'D', has the tritet 0b010, which the stream-start table reserves for a text-domain op code ('_'); 'D' is neither an op code nor a count code, and no field map or annotation starts with it, so the stream does not resume with any of the eight permitted frames. The specification states no parser-side rule for this stream; the stream breaks the cited MUST, and the assertion that a parser rejects it is graded SHOULD on the inference recorded in inferred_from.

cases.title: Reject a body shorter than its version string declares
cases.description: A KERI 2.0 inception with the last five bytes of the stream removed, so the body is shorter than the size its version string declares. The adapter protocol makes the end of the input final (a harness rule, not a specification claim), so a parser may not wait for more bytes. Line 1129 requires a parser to extract a field map by the size its version string declares, which it cannot do for a body shorter than that.

assertions.note: Relies on the adapter protocol's end-of-input rule. Informative class: truncated.
